subject: Signed artifact & runtime image playbook for partner marketplace integration
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@lumenmodels.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Marketplace integration — artifact signing & runtime images proposal

Hi Jonas / Camila / Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited by the alignment. LumenModel Labs is preparing a small catalog of community-published models we want to make available via Redwood's partner marketplace. Before we proceed we'd like to align on a lightweight, auditable artifact exchange workflow so customers can verify provenance and so Redwood can safely host runtime images that include quantized weights.

High-level asks from our side:
- Signed model artifacts (detached signature + checksum manifest) for each published weight bundle.
- Signed runtime images (OCI manifest) with reproducible builds; we can provide a Dockerfile + build steps.
- Minimal metadata schema: model name, version, training checksum, license pointer, rerun instructions.
- A mirror policy: we want the ability to host mirrors (third-party mirrors such as MirrorBox) when geography / egress costs warrant it, but require signed artifacts and a timestamped provenance record.

I've attached a short one-page sketch of our suggested artifact signing layout and a sample manifest (artifact-signing-spec-v1.pdf). Would Redwood have any must-have constraints (e.g., KMS/HSM signing, signature algorithm, manifest format) or ingestion requirements for the marketplace?

Proposed next step: a short call to align on technical requirements and the legal/weights-access checkbox (we expect to keep weights under an open-model license but need clarity on redistribution permissions). Are you available Wed/Thu this week?

Cheers,
Elena Rossi
Head of Partnerships — LumenModel Labs
elena@lumenmodels.ai

Attachment: artifact-signing-spec-v1.pdf (1 page sketch)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@lumenmodels.ai>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 10:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace integration — artifact signing & runtime images proposal

Elena — thanks for the clear note and the spec sketch. This is the kind of integration we want to standardize for publisher alliances. Quick answers up front:

- Signing: Redwood prefers an HSM-backed signing flow for any artifacts we host directly. We can accept detached signatures (PEM) or sigstore/cosign bundles; we use ECDSA-P256 by default but can support RSA-4096 for backward compatibility.
- Manifests: JSON manifest with canonical key ordering; we also publish a canonical digest (sha256) in our catalog.
- Ingestion: a signed manifest + object checksum + provenance record (who/when/how) is required. We also support a GitHub-based SLSA attestation flow if publishers want automated provenance.
- Mirrors: we can support third-party mirrors provided the mirror hosts the verified signed artifacts and we have an allowlist + signed mirror manifest. The mirror must replicate signatures and not re-sign artifacts.

I've attached a short Redwood draft called "artifact-signing-spec-v1.pdf" with our preferred fields and an example of how we store the metadata. Two asks from our side: (1) we need clarity on the license header you expect to ship with the weights (copy of license text or SPDX id) and (2) we need a contact point on your side for the signature key rotation window.

Can Camila and Sergio join a 30-minute call Thu Mar 4 at 11:00 PT?

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Alliances — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Attachment: runtime-image-manifest-example.tar.gz (contains example OCI manifest + README)
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>

Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 18:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Marketplace integration — artifact signing & runtime images proposal

Elena/Team — thanks, joined the call this morning with engineering and security to walk the draft. A few practical notes and proposed guardrails we want to capture in the partner playbook (short bullets):

- Required metadata: SPDX license identifier, training dataset pointer (high-level), model card URL, sha256(weights), build environment hash.
- Access controls: Redwood will host the weights under the publisher's indicated license. For any redistribution beyond mirror replication (e.g., fork/repackaging), we require explicit permission or an attribution clause in the license.
- Runtime images: Redwood will prefer OCI image signatures (cosign) and store attestation links in the model catalog. We will not accept images that modify weights at runtime without a new signed manifest.
- Key management: we expect partners to rotate signing keys with a 90-day notice window; Redwood can support cross-signed rollovers if Lumen wants to use your KMS.
- Escrow / escrow-less path: for higher-risk models customers may request escrowed weights; alternatively we can provide a reproducible-build attestation and runtime verification (signing + SBOM).

Action items from our side: Camila to draft partner playbook text and a short legal checklist for the redistribution/attribution clause; Jonas to capture the technical schema and add to the GitHub repo. Elena — can you confirm the license you plan to use (SPDX id preferred) and provide a point of contact for your security lead for key rotation details?

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Sr. Partner Ops — Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.com

Thanks everyone — follow-up from our side after today's call. We've attached a signed LOI covering the pilot scope (Lumen first three models, MirrorBox mirror replication, standard Apache-2.0 weights license) and a short contact list. Key points:

- License: Apache-2.0 (SPDX: Apache-2.0) for the pilot; we will surface any third-party dataset terms if relevant.
- Signing: we'll generate cosign-compatible signatures and publish detached sigs alongside manifests. Lumen will maintain the private signing key in our KMS and share a public key; we'll notify Redwood 14 days prior to any rotation.
- Mirrors: MirrorBox will host identical objects and replicate signatures; Redwood's allowlist requirement is acceptable.

Next steps we propose:
1) Redwood to merge the artifact schema PR (Jonas) into the artifact-specs repo and publish a short ingestion guide.
2) Camila to share partner playbook draft and legal checklist by Friday Mar 12.
3) Lumen to upload first signed artifacts to the sandbox bucket and notify Redwood security.

We're attaching the signed LOI: Lumen_LOI_signed.pdf. Please confirm once you've got the artifacts ingestion guide live and we'll start the sandbox push.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Partnerships — LumenModel Labs
elena@lumenmodels.ai
